title: Two-Step Equations Notes + Maze Activity (All Things Algebra)

gaps: maze-activity: navigational puzzle where correct answers determine the path — requires procedural maze generation tied to problem solutions
guided-notes: two-column notes page with main-ideas/questions column on left and notes/examples column on right, progressive scaffolding from review to new concept

components.name: Guided Notes (pages 1-2)
components.description: Cornell-style two-column layout. Left column: topic labels (One-Step Equations, Fractions, Two-Step Equations, Watch Out!). Right column: worked examples with blank spaces for student work. Progressive difficulty: one-step → fractions → two-step → special cases (coefficient before variable). 22 problems total.
designPatterns: Progressive scaffolding: starts with review (one-step) before introducing new concept (two-step)
Fill-in-the-blank strategy cues: 'To get rid of a fraction, multiply by the ___'
Watch Out! section for common traps (division before subtraction)
Student header block: Name, Class, Date, Topic

components.name: Maze Activity (page 3)
components.description: Grid-based maze where students solve two-step equations and follow the correct answer to navigate from START to END. 13 problems embedded in maze cells. Wrong answers lead to dead ends. Multiple-choice format via maze paths (each cell connects to 2-3 numbered exits).
designPatterns: Gamification: transforms drill practice into navigation challenge
Self-checking: wrong answer = dead end = immediate feedback
Show-all-steps requirement enforces process over guessing
Answer options visible on paths create low-stakes multiple-choice feel

notes: Three-page bundle from All Things Algebra (Gina Wilson). Strong pedagogical structure — the notes page teaches the concept with graduated difficulty, then the maze provides gamified practice. The maze format is the standout: it's essentially self-checking drill practice disguised as a puzzle. This is a new format type for Homa — neither pure worksheet nor pure game.
